reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let Omega be a measurable space with finite measure mu, F a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, T>0, and J a finite type. For each j in J let B_j:NNReal x Omega->R be a scalar Brownian motion with F: centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B_j(t)-B_j(s) from F_s whenever s<=t. No mutual independence between the B_j is assumed. Usual conditions mean every mu-null set is in every F_t and F is right-continuous. Let eta_j and xi_j be real strongly progressive L2 integrands on mu product lambda_T, with lambda_T the transported Lebesgue measure on [0,T]. For any such family h let R_h(t)=sum_j I^T_{B_j}(h_j)(t), where each integral is the specified continuous completed Ito version, patched to zero on its exceptional null set and held constant after T. Let n in N and let t_0,...,t_n be any nondecreasing NNReal times with t_n<=T. Define Q_h(omega)=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(R_h(t_{i+1},omega)-R_h(t_i,omega))^2. Then Q_eta-Q_xi is mu-integrable and
integral |Q_eta-Q_xi| dmu <= real(card J)*sqrt(sum_j ||eta_j+xi_j||_{L2(mu product lambda_T)}^2)*sqrt(sum_j ||eta_j-xi_j||_{L2(mu product lambda_T)}^2).
The plus/minus integrands are defined pointwise by eta_j(t,omega) plus/minus xi_j(t,omega); their toLp values are precisely the L2 equivalence classes of the associated (omega,t)-functions. No condition t_0=0 or t_n=T is imposed.
objects: Omega,mu,F,T; finite J; scalar Brownian family B_j; integrand families eta,xi; arbitrary nondecreasing finite grid; sum-of-integrals processes R_h; quadratic sums Q_h; L2 classes of eta_j plus/minus xi_j.
domains: J finite, with no DecidableEq instance required; time NNReal; scalar real stochastic integrals; L2 on Omega x NNReal with mu product lambda_T; n natural including zero.
quantifiers: For every finite measure space and scalar Brownian family with common usual filtration and positive horizon, every eta,xi and every nondecreasing grid ending at or before T, both integrability and inequality hold.
assumptions: mu finite; T>0; each B_j scalar Brownian with F; usual conditions; eta_j and xi_j progressive L2; grid monotone and last time<=T. No cross-driver independence assumption.
conclusion: Integrability of Q_eta-Q_xi and the specified L1 bound involving card J and the two sums of squared L2 norms.
scopes: Finite deterministic grid, arbitrary initial time and possible repeated times; every Ito process uses its corresponding B_j. Exact inequality, no limit statement.
constant_dependencies: Only explicit multiplicative constant is real(card J); norms use the fixed full-horizon product measure and depend on eta,xi,mu,T. Bound does not depend on grid size or individual grid locations beyond the horizon conditions.
